notes: The spec's testing protocol -- 'Select 50 random start dates with an available 52-week forward horizon; for each date, run a separate backtest' and 'report the average values of the metrics across all 50 runs' -- is unseeded randomness plus a 50-run Monte-Carlo evaluation that cannot map to one behavioral tape under the bench's single-backtest harness ('other' class), and it leaves the entry trigger ('On the selected start date, buy') unpinned. Secondary: 'every 12 weeks' rebalance and 'at the end of 52 weeks' exit on the bound AAPL 1d feed (weekly 'resampling from daily data if needed') admit divergent boundary conversions (52 weekly resampled bars vs 260 trading days vs 364 calendar days), shifting fill timestamps. Sizing (100% of portfolio) and commission (0.1%, matching the bench's 0.001) are pinned; no indicators; prose is generic single-asset so the AAPL binding is coherent; no hardcoded price levels.
